text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- President Hosni Mubarak said Egypt supports the peace process to the utmost. "The European envoy does not have the right to give Egypt a deadline for achieving progress in the peace process. We give him two years to see what he can do," he added on a tour of oil facilities in Fayyoum.
He said relations with the United States were strong and Egypt consults with it on every move in the peace process.
- Mubarak had phone calls on the peace process from King Hussein of Jordan and French President Jacques Chirac.
- Mubarak will chair a meeting of the Supreme Committee for Exports on July 1.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will chair a meeting of nine ministers today to study a report from Industry Minister Soleiman Reda on developing Egyptian-Libyan economic relations, in the light of the recent visit of an Egyptian delegation.
- In the months of April and May investment offices in the provinces received applications to set up 473 projects with a total investment of about 4.7 billion pounds ($1.38 billion).
AL-AKHBAR
- Mubarak said the future promises plenty of petroleum. Oil companies have made 17 discoveries this year and reserves have risen to 1.177 billion tonnes.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said the Middle East peace process requires more effort in the coming days. He said the gap between the Israeli and Palestinian sides remained.

- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali said deliveries of wheat by farmers were 65 percent above the levels of last year because the farmers receive an advance payment immediately. Agricultural cooperatives have received 164,000 tonnes so far.
- The Supreme State Security Coirt extended for 45 days the detention of alleged Egyptian spy Samir Osman.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Mubarak said an Arab common market was the only way for the Arab nation to build its economy.

- It has been decided to apply the voluntary early retirement scheme next month to workers in seven ailing contracting companies which are subsidiaries of the state's National Company for Construction and Development.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid decided to sell two state companies -- Industrial Installations and Services and Nasr Castings -- to the employees in instalments over 10 years, with a grace period of three years.
- The big Egyptian newspapers have gone on sale in Libya for the first time in two years. Sales had been suspended for administrative reasons.
$1 = 3.395 pounds
